definition: Deep reinforcement learning (deep RL) is a subfield of machine learning that combines reinforcement learning (RL) and deep learning.
details: RL considers the problem of a computational agent learning to make decisions by trial and error. Deep RL incorporates deep learning into the solution, allowing agents to make decisions from unstructured input data without manual engineering of the state space. Deep RL algorithms are able to take in very large inputs (e.g. every pixel rendered to the screen in a video game) and decide what actions to perform to optimize an objective (e.g. maximizing the game score). Deep reinforcement learning has been used for a diverse set of applications including but not limited to robotics, video games, natural language processing, computer vision, education, transportation, finance and healthcare.

explainer.lead: Deep reinforcement learning teaches a computer to make decisions through trial and error, using deep learning to handle raw, complicated inputs such as game-screen pixels. It matters because people do not have to manually reduce those inputs to a tidy set of features before the agent can learn.

tiers.eli5: Imagine learning a video game by trying different buttons and seeing what raises your score. Deep reinforcement learning works similarly: a computer tries actions, learns from the results, and gradually gets better. It can look directly at the screen instead of needing someone to explain every important detail first.
tiers.practitioner: Use deep RL when an agent must choose actions from large or unstructured observations and has an objective to optimize, such as a game score. The deep-learning component replaces manual state-space engineering, allowing very large inputs to feed directly into decision making.
tiers.paperLevel: Deep RL combines reinforcement learning, in which a computational agent learns decisions by trial and error, with deep learning. It learns action selection from high-dimensional unstructured inputs while optimizing an objective, such as maximizing game score.

explainer.example: In a video game, the agent takes every pixel rendered on the screen as input and decides which game action to perform. Over repeated attempts, it learns decisions intended to maximize the game score.

explainer.intuition: Learn by doing, but let a deep-learning system interpret the messy observations. Instead of a person designing a compact description of the situation, the agent can work from inputs as large as an entire video-game frame.
howItWorks: The agent receives an unstructured or very large input describing its situation.
It chooses an action to perform.
Through trial and error, it learns which decisions better serve its objective.
Deep learning enables this process without manually engineering the state space.
explainer.whyItMatters: Deep RL makes trial-and-error learning practical with inputs that would otherwise require extensive manual state-space design. Its applications span robotics, video games, natural language processing, computer vision, education, transportation, finance, and healthcare.
misconceptions: It is not just deep learning: the decision-making agent also learns through trial and error.
It is not limited to video games; those are simply a clear example among many application areas.
